research_mode: official Home Office, ONS and OSR sources only; outcome 14-22 definitions, CSEW response/reporting and weighting, police-recorded revision/QA, comparability and governance controls; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: CSEW comparable-crime reporting proportion
verified_claims: ONS estimates that around 42 percent of CSEW-comparable crimes were reported by the public to police in YE March 2026
police recorded crime therefore omits many unreported offences
the estimate concerns comparable CSEW crimes
limitations: 42 percent is not applicable to every offence type
the proportion is not a local reporting rate

sources.name: Offence-specific reporting variation
verified_claims: the proportion reported to police varies considerably by offence type
recorded-crime fitness depends on reporting as well as recording
aggregate reporting proportions can conceal offence differences
limitations: a national average must not be assigned to each offence
reporting variation is not proof of force under-recording

sources.name: Police-recorded local pattern use
verified_claims: police recorded crime can be used for local crime pattern analysis
it is useful for well-reported and well-recorded offences
homicide is a key example not covered by CSEW
limitations: local pattern use still requires geography and recording-quality controls
it does not support exact parcel attribution by itself

sources.name: Police workload indicator
verified_claims: recorded crime is an important indicator of police workload
it shows where policing effort is being spent
workload interpretation is distinct from victimisation prevalence
limitations: high workload is not automatically high underlying crime
recording and enforcement activity affect workload measures

sources.name: Police-activity-sensitive offences
verified_claims: drug-possession recorded volumes are heavily influenced by police activity and priorities
for such offences recorded crime can indicate enforcement activity
the measure may not reflect underlying criminality directly
limitations: activity-sensitive categories must not be compared as pure prevalence
policy changes can create discontinuities

sources.name: CSEW independent-check role
verified_claims: CSEW includes offences not reported to or recorded by police
it is widely viewed as an independent check on police figures
responsibility transferred from the Home Office to ONS in April 2012
limitations: CSEW has its own scope exclusions and sampling errors
independence does not make sources interchangeable

sources.name: CSEW long-term trend role
verified_claims: for covered crimes and populations CSEW is a better long-term trend indicator than police recorded crime
it is unaffected by changes in police counting rules
it is also unaffected by changes in reporting and recording practice
limitations: the statement does not apply to crimes outside CSEW coverage
questionnaire changes still require measure-version checks

sources.name: CSEW main-estimate exclusions
verified_claims: the main CSEW estimate excludes homicide
it excludes crimes against businesses and drug possession
sexual offences are excluded from the main face-to-face crime estimate
limitations: excluded crimes must not be represented as zero
other sources or separate modules are required

sources.name: CSEW sensitive self-completion module
verified_claims: people aged 16 or over complete a separate tablet module on domestic and sexual violence
these results are reported separately
the module reduces pressure to disclose sensitive experiences to an interviewer
limitations: self-completion outputs have separate definitions and bases
they must not be silently merged into headline crime

sources.name: CSEW fraud-question introduction
verified_claims: fraud and computer-misuse questions were added in October 2015
sufficient data were available for first publication in July 2016
the estimates entered headline crime after a full interview year
limitations: pre-2015 headline series did not include these questions
series comparisons require the fraud-coverage boundary
